title: This Seal Dives 2,000 Feet, but Its Teeth Are the Problem
subject: Weddell seal

scenes.text: This seal dives 2,000 feet. Its teeth are the problem.
Weddell seals live under Antarctic sea ice that can freeze solid.
They need air. So they scrape breathing holes with their teeth.
They can stay under for up to 80 minutes and dive about 600 meters.
But grinding ice wears the teeth down. Worn teeth are thought to be a common cause of death.
A seal that dives 2,000 feet can be beaten by ice.

description:
A Weddell seal can dive about 600 meters, but its teeth are its weak spot.
It scrapes breathing holes in sea ice, and the wear is thought to be a common cause of death.
Would you trust your teeth with this job?
